request_context: A request to turn an approved requirements document and an existing system-level architecture into a design for one feature, detailed enough for a developer to build from.

rules.source_quote: Each requirement from `requirements.md` MUST map to at least one component in the design
rules.outcome: Every requirement in the input is handled by at least one named component of the design, and the design says which requirements it covers.
rules.why: Gaps between what was asked and what is designed show up at design time instead of during build.
rules.scenario_hint: The requirements list includes a cross-cutting item that is easy to overlook, such as audit logging or data deletion.

rules.source_quote: If a requirement cannot be addressed by the design, flag it explicitly
rules.outcome: A requirement that the design cannot meet, or that conflicts with the supplied architecture, is called out openly instead of being left out or assumed to be satisfied.
rules.why: A silent gap becomes a surprise late in the project.
rules.scenario_hint: One requirement needs real-time updates but the supplied architecture only processes data in nightly batches.

rules.source_quote: reference them but do not duplicate their full design
rules.outcome: Only the components the feature needs are designed in detail. Parts owned by the wider system or by another feature, such as sign-in checks, logging or another feature's entities, are referred to and built upon, not redesigned or copied.
rules.why: Copied designs drift apart and bury the feature's own decisions.
rules.scenario_hint: The system architecture covers many features and the user wants a design for just one that reuses shared parts.

rules.source_quote: Component interfaces use typed signatures (not vague descriptions)
rules.outcome: Each component's public operations are given with parameter and return types, not only described in prose.
rules.why: A developer can start coding against a concrete contract and reviewers can check it.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request for a feature design that includes services or modules with several operations.

rules.source_quote: Data models include field types and constraints
rules.outcome: Stored and exchanged data structures list each field with its type and its constraints, such as required or optional, allowed values, format and key role.
rules.why: Ambiguous data shapes cause mismatches between components and in storage.
rules.scenario_hint: The feature stores records in a database and exposes them through an API.

rules.outcome: Failure cases are covered for invalid input, missing or insufficient permission, missing resources, conflicting concurrent changes, failures of outside services and request throttling, wherever the feature can meet them.
rules.why: Unplanned failure paths are where most production defects hide.
rules.scenario_hint: The feature accepts user input, calls another service and writes to shared data.

rules.outcome: For each failure case the design says what the user or caller sees and whether the system retries, falls back or escalates.
rules.why: Naming the failure is not enough; the build team needs to know the intended behaviour.
rules.scenario_hint: The feature depends on an outside service that can time out or be rate limited.

rules.source_quote: Testing strategy missing one of the three levels (unit, integration, E2E)
rules.outcome: The test approach separates what is checked in isolation, what is checked across component interactions and which end-to-end user journeys are checked, with concrete example cases.
rules.why: Each level catches different defects and concrete cases make the plan actionable.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request for a feature design that should include how the feature will be tested.

rules.source_quote: Scope boundaries — what is and is not included
rules.outcome: The design states what is in and out of scope and gives the reasons for its main design choices.
rules.why: Readers can judge the choices and know what was left for later.
rules.scenario_hint: The requirements leave room for several designs, such as sync versus async processing.

rules.source_quote: A developer reading only this design.md (plus requirements.md) should understand what to build
rules.outcome: The design is self-contained: a developer with only the requirements and this design can tell what to build without needing extra context.
rules.why: A design that depends on unwritten knowledge cannot be handed over.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request for a feature design.

rules.source_quote: Mermaid diagrams (SHOULD include at least one)
rules.outcome: The design includes at least one diagram that shows how the components interact or how a request flows through them.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request for a feature design.

rules.source_quote: Every `design.md` MUST contain exactly these 6 sections in this order
rules.outcome: The design opens with a summary of the feature, then covers its architecture, the components with their interfaces, the data structures, the error cases and the test approach, in that order.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request for a feature design.
